title: The Fall Edit
note: Three pieces that earned it. Chosen for the cut first, then held to the same composition standard as everything else here.

picks.note: Fifty percent wool, forty-nine percent alpaca, one percent polyamide holding the seams. The alpaca is what gives it drape instead of bulk.
Cashmere and nothing else. The funnel neck is the part that makes it work without a scarf.
Full lambskin, and it will crease where you sit. Vince says lined without saying with what, so we say that rather than guess.

heading: We read the label so you don’t have to.
body: Every piece here has been through the same check. Shell composition and lining composition, pulled apart, parsed into percentages, and shown on the card before you click anything. No scrolling to the bottom of a product page to find out what you are actually buying.

title: Wedding Guest, Read Properly
note: Wedding guest is where composition gets worst, because beading and structure usually mean polyester doing the work underneath. These three do not.

picks.note: Cotton and silk on top, one hundred percent silk lining underneath. Nothing else in the catalog does both.
Ninety-six percent wool with four percent elastane for the shape. Inside our allowance, and the crepe is why it hangs like that.
Cotton and silk with three percent metallic yarn doing the shimmer. Rare for anything that catches light.

heading: The lining is where it hides.
body: A wool crepe dress with a polyester lining breathes like polyester. Most sites fold the lining into one composition line, or leave it off entirely. We show it separately on every card, and you can filter on it.

title: What Satin Isn’t
by: Three pieces that read like silk
note: Satin is a weave, not a fiber. It is the single most expensive thing most people do not know about buying clothes. Each of these looks like silk on the hanger and none of them is.
cta: See what one hundred percent looks like

picks.note: Ninety-nine percent rayon with a polyester contrast. Honestly sold as satin, because satin describes how it was woven.
One hundred percent viscose. Plant derived, chemically rebuilt, and it will not breathe like the silk it resembles.
One hundred percent nylon at a Net-a-Porter price. The crystals are the reason, and we still think you should know.

heading: Natural is not the same as sustainable.
body: Composition tells you how a garment will feel, wear and age. It does not tell you how the animal was treated, who sewed it, or what the dye house released. Those are real questions and we do not pretend a percentage answers them.
